To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

global signal regression (1) alters correlations within a group; (2) can alter correlations differently between groups; (3) can alter local and global correlations; (4) can spread group differences to regions never having any; (5) should not be used to study group differences in resting-state functional MRI (RS-FMRI); and (6) should be replaced with careful accounting of nuisance variables.

GSReg can distort the correlation structure of the data in such a way that group differences in correlation patterns are not necessarily due to group differences in the underlying brain functional connectivity.
